34.23.7.en: It is well said by the prophet: "He casteth the wicked down to the ground" (Ps 147:6). For since they lose heavenly things, all they thirst for is earthly, and everything they pursue and that seems greater to them, they seek through it what is lower in value.

34.23.8.en: It is well said of them by Jeremiah: [They that depart from thee shall be written in the earth] (see Jer 17:13). While on the other side it is said of the elect: "Rather rejoice, because your names are written in heaven" (Lk 10:20).

34.24.0.en: Therefore he knoweth their works, and he overturneth them in the night, so that they are destroyed [25].

34.24.1.en: God knows their works, and what they plan, without need of examination; so He gives them many opportunities, perhaps they will turn back from evil, and in a single night He shatters them. Clear examples in the Old Testament are what happened to all of Egypt's people when all the firstborn died in one night, and also Belshazzar king of Babylon (Dan 5:30).

34.24.2.en: "He overturneth them in the night": the literal translation is "He overturns the night." That is, He turns it upon them, so that a grave disaster they do not expect befalls them. The word "night" often indicates an unexpected disaster, hard to face.

34.24.3.en: * It is understood in particular that every wicked man is crushed in the night in two ways: either when he is struck from outside with the torment of punishment, or when he is stricken with a sentence, when he loses forever the light of life by the final judgment. As it is written: "Bind him hand and foot, and take him away, and cast him into outer darkness" (Mt 22:13). Then he is sent by force into the outer darkness, since by his own will he has become blind with the inner darkness...

34.24.4.en: Every sin that is not quickly wiped out by remorse is either a sin and the cause of a sin, or a sin and a punishment for a sin.

34.24.5.en: The sin that remorse does not wash away at once leads, by its weight, to another sin. So it is not only a sin, but in addition it is the cause of a sin.

34.24.6.en: This sin is followed by the stirring up of faults, as the blind mind is led to suffer slavery from sin to another sin(b); but the sin that arises from a sin does not merely return after the sin, but becomes a sin with the punishment of a sin added.

34.25.0.en: He striketh them as wicked men in the open sight of others [26].

34.25.1.en: The wicked often want to disappear from sight as in darkness, because their works are darkness that cannot bear the light; therefore the Lord chastises them openly so that they tremble and realize their inability to escape the divine justice, and so that they become a practical lesson to others, who will not imitate them.

34.25.2.en: Perhaps Elihu was fixing his eyes on the calamities that had befallen Job in public.

34.25.3.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) holds that the onlookers are the godly who stand as witnesses against the wicked on the day of judgment.

34.25.4.en: * "He striketh them as wicked men in the open sight of others" (Job 34:26)...

34.25.5.en: Holy Scripture calls unbelievers in particular wicked. For sinners are distinguished from the wicked by this difference: every wicked man is a sinner, but not every sinner is wicked. For even a man who is godly in the faith can be a sinner. John says: "If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us" (1 Jn 1:8). But a man is rightly called wicked if he is estranged from the holiness of religion... The very calm of the Church's peace hides many under the Christian name and the plague of their wickedness envelops them. But when they are struck by a light breath of persecution, it sweeps them away at once like chaff from the threshing floor.

34.25.6.en: Some people desire to bear the mark of the Christian calling, because the name of Christ has been exalted, so that nearly everyone looks to appear as believers. When they see others called so, they are ashamed to appear unbelievers, but they neglect to become what they boast of being called...

34.25.7.en: Some keep the faith inside their hearts, but they do not care to walk faithfully in life... Since they ignore the exacting life, they fall into unbelief without anyone persecuting them... These are hidden from the eyes of men but exposed in the sight of God.

34.25.8.en: Many die unbelieving while dwelling in the faith itself. It is rightly said: "He striketh them as wicked men in the open sight of others" (Job 34:26). For they show themselves before men in the Church as godly persons, but since they cannot escape the divine judgments, they are struck as wicked men.

34.26.0.en: Because they turned back from him, and would not consider any of his ways [27].

34.26.1.en: He gives an explanation for their chastisement in public, namely their forsaking of the Holy God in secret, within their hearts and thoughts as in their hidden conduct, and they did not accept the way of the Lord, that is, they did not keep His commandments nor give any consideration to God Himself in their lives.

34.26.2.en: * "Because they turned back from him, and would not consider any of his ways" [27]. What will befall the wicked on the day of judgment has its secret in their turning away from God, or turning back from him, and their indifference to His divine ways.

34.26.3.en: * [Who turned aside from him, as if deliberately]. We should understand that sin is committed in three ways: either from ignorance, or from weakness, or deliberately.

34.26.4.en: Our sin becomes graver if it is from weakness and not from ignorance, but the danger is greater if it is deliberate and not from weakness.

34.26.5.en: Paul sinned from ignorance when he said: "Who was before a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and injurious: but I obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief" (1 Tim 1:13).

34.26.6.en: Peter sinned from weakness when the word of the maid shook the strength of the faith he had spoken of with the Lord, and when he denied with his voice the Lord whom he held fast in his heart (Mt 26:69).

34.26.7.en: But those sinned deliberately of whom the Lord Himself said: "If I had not come and spoken unto them, they had not had sin: but now they have no cloke for their sin" (Jn 15:22). To sin deliberately means that you do not love goodness and do not do it. Therefore sometimes the guilt is heavier to love sin than to practice it. Likewise it is a greater sin to hate righteousness than not to do it. Therefore there are some in the Church who are far from goodness and even persecute it, and also those who hate in others what they themselves practice in negligence.

34.26.8.en: * [And would not consider any of his ways]. He does not say that they do not understand from weakness, but that they do not want to understand, because men often despise the knowledge of things which they greatly boast of doing... since they reckon that their ignorance of them gives them immunity concerning their sins...

34.26.9.en: To understand the ways of the Lord is to bear with humility the passing things (afflictions) and to wait with steadfastness for the abiding things (the eternal things).

34.27.0.en: So that they cause the cry of the poor to come unto him, and he heareth the cry of the afflicted [28].

34.27.1.en: By forsaking the way of the Lord and rejecting His commandments, they opened the way for the cries of the poor whom they wronged to ascend to the Lord, and the cries of the afflicted (the sorrowful) to reach Him. In other words, when the wicked man rejects the way of the Lord and stops his ears from hearing the divine commandment in his practical life, he causes loss and bitterness to his brethren, so their cries ascend to heaven and reach the ears of God.

34.27.2.en: There is nothing more terrifying in the heavenly court than the hardness of man's heart toward his brother because of his rejection of the commandment of divine love. For even if he prays to God, He stops His ears until man opens his ears to those whom he has grieved and troubled. For the tears and sighs of the sufferers go before and complain against the wicked wrongdoers.

34.27.3.en: * [So that the cry of the needy comes to him, and he hears the voice of the poor] [28]. While these (the wicked) boast, those whom they oppress cry out to God, or it certainly means that they cause the cry of the poor to reach God... This also refers to the leaders of the Church who cease from the work of preaching and busy themselves with worldly concerns. They leave the obligations of preaching. By this they oblige the flock under them to rush into complaint and murmuring. Everyone whom you urge complains, as if with justice, of the conduct of the false shepherd, asking: Why does one who does not practice the work occupy the place of the teacher?

34.27.5.en: When he giveth quietness, who then can make trouble?

34.28.0.en: And when he hideth his face, who then can behold him? whether it be done against a nation, or against a man only? [29]

34.28.1.en: Elihu says: {When God hears the groans of the people and the sighs of the suffering man, He gives rest or comfort or prosperity to the poor, the suffering and the wronged; then who dares to cause them trouble or hardship?} Elihu wants to affirm that all things are under His authority, He hears the voice of the sufferers and acts, and the wicked, with all their abilities and authority, cannot touch them!

34.28.2.en: "And when he hideth his face" is a biblical expression indicating the coming of a disaster, as though announcing that God has hidden His face from man, so no one can see him, that is, care for him and lift from him the disaster that has befallen him, and give him peace and joy.

34.28.3.en: It is as though Elihu invites Job to return to God, for He alone, when He gives him divine comfort and inner peace, can keep trials and men's troubles from harming him. But if he does not return to God, He will hide His face from him, and all the faces of men cannot look upon him and give him rest.

34.28.4.en: This principle, that the secret of man's rest is in God's hand and not in men's, applies to the people as a whole as well as to the individual person.

34.28.5.en: If God justifies us by His love, no one can condemn us, and if He is angry with us, no one can give us peace! Then let us enjoy perfect peace by centering our depths on God, the source of peace and the gladdener of hearts (Prov 16:7; Isa 26:3).

34.28.6.en: * [When he giveth peace, who then can condemn? and when he hideth his face, who then can behold him?] [29]... He also says this when He gives the laborers in the vineyard their wages... "Didst not thou agree with me for a penny?... I will give unto this last, even as unto thee. Is it not lawful for me to do what I will with mine own?" (see Mt 20:13-15)...

34.28.7.en: "Whether it be done against a nation, or against a man only"... The divine judgments are set forth in the same manner concerning one soul or one city, and also concerning one city or one nation, and in the same manner concerning the human race. The Lord cares for particular persons in the same manner as He cares for the whole world.

34.28.8.en: Again, He directs His care toward all at the same time as if He did not care for individuals. For He who fills all things by His providence fills all. And when He cares for one thing alone, He is at the same time present in all. Again, while He governs the whole world, He is present with each individual. In fact, He does everything by the power of His nature without moving. What is marvelous is that while He is intent on something, He is not limited by it, He who works even while at rest.

34.29.0.en: That the hypocrite (the ungodly) reign not, lest the people be ensnared [30].

34.29.1.en: All human affairs are in the hand of God, under His surpassing care, so that the wicked hypocrite may not reign and rule over his brethren, thinking himself possessor of irresistible authority, with no one able to restrain him or check him from wronging them. And lest this wicked man become a snare into which the people fall, as they feel as though God does not care about the injustice that has come upon them.

34.29.2.en: So it is fitting for leaders - at all levels - to realize that though they have received authority, God is above all, the controller of all. The psalmist says: "For the rod of the wicked shall not rest upon the lot of the righteous; lest the righteous put forth their hands unto iniquity" (Ps 125:3).

34.29.3.en: * "Who makes the hypocrite reign for the sins of the people" [30]. Judea did not want the true King to reign over her, so she brought a hypocrite to reign over her as befitted her deserts. As the Truth Himself says in the Gospel: [I am come in my Father's name, and ye receive me not: if another shall come in his own name, him ye will receive] (Jn 5:43). Paul says: "Because they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved. And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie" (2 Thess 2:10-11).

34.29.4.en: By saying: [Who makes the hypocrite reign for the sins of the people] he perhaps means the Antichrist, the chief of all hypocrites. For the deceiver pretends to holiness in order to draw men to evil...

34.29.5.en: This Antichrist reigns over the wicked, not because of the injustice of the judge, but because of the sin of those who are obliged to bear the punishment. Although most of them do not see his ruling power, they are enslaved to him because of the state they have reached by their sins. Without doubt they honor him by their wicked lives, these who do not see his tyranny over them. Are these not his members who seek, by displaying holiness, what they are not...? For it is written: "Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin" (Jn 8:34). For to the extent that they commit sins by this will of theirs which they desire, they bow down to the service of (the Antichrist), enslaved to him.

34.29.6.en: May whoever suffers under such a ruler not blame the wicked ruler... but blame the faults of his own wicked deeds and not the injustice of his ruler. It is written: "I gave thee a king in mine anger" (Hos 13:11).

34.29.7.en: Why then do we mock the one who is set up as ruler over us, who received his authority from God's wrath? If we receive rulers according to our deserts from God's displeasure, we infer from their conduct what our own condition truly is...! The characteristics of rulers are fixed according to the deserts of those subject to them. Even those who appear to be good are changed by the power they receive. Observe Scripture! Saul's very heart changed with his dignity. It is written: "When thou wast little in thine own sight, wast thou not made the head of the tribes of Israel?" (1 Sam 15:17).

34.29.8.en: The conduct of rulers is shaped according to the characteristics of those subject to them, for the conduct of even a good shepherd becomes evil because of the evil of his flock.

34.29.10.en: * The wicked are scattered bitterly like light tares, but the righteous are saved like heavy wheat. So note what the Lord says to Peter: "Behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat: but I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not" (Lk 22:31-32). Those who are scattered like tares perish, but he who does not perish is like the seed that falls and grows and increases and brings forth much fruit (Lk 8:8)... Evil is likened to the chaff that burns quickly and becomes dust.

34.29.11.en: St. Ambrose * Here is the remedy for your sickness: "Fret not thyself because of him who prospereth in his way"(c). Yes, he prospers, but in his own way. But you labor, yet in the way of God.

34.29.12.en: He travels on his journey recklessly, but where is he going?

34.29.13.en: If Christ had promised you the good things of this world, you would have reason to be angry, because the unbeliever overflows in his ways.

34.29.14.en: What has He promised you? Eternal happiness when the dead are raised, and in this life He promised you His own portion. I repeat, His portion is the way that He walked. Do you despise what your Master walked, you who are a servant and disciple? You have heard that the servant is not better than his master, for He suffered! A thing which that Righteous One did not deserve, so what do you deserve, O sinner?

34.29.15.en: * "For the rod of the wicked shall not rest upon the lot of the righteous; lest the righteous put forth their hands unto iniquity" (Ps 125:3). At present the righteous suffer to some extent, and at present the wicked sometimes oppress the righteous. In what ways? Sometimes the wicked attain temporal honors, and when they attain them and become judges or kings, God permits this for the chastening of His flock, for the chastening of His people; here the honor that befits them must be shown... And sometimes there are authorities who are good and fear God, and some of them have no fear of God in them.

34.29.16.en: Julian was an unbelieving emperor, an apostate, wicked and an idol worshiper. And the Christian soldiers served an unbelieving emperor.... Whenever he called them to worship idols and offer incense to them they pointed to God, but when he commanded them to deploy in the lines of soldiers and move against this nation or that, they obeyed at once. They distinguished between their eternal Master and their temporal master, and for the sake of their eternal Master they submitted to the temporal. But do the wicked always hold authority over the righteous? The rod of the wicked remains for a time upon the lot of the righteous, but it will not last forever. A time will come when Christ will appear in His glory and gather all the nations before Him.

34.30.0.en: 31 "Surely it is meet to be said unto God, I have borne chastisement, I will not offend any more: 32 That which I see not teach thou me: if I have done iniquity, I will do no more. 33 Should it be according to thy mind? he will recompense it, whether thou refuse, or whether thou choose; and not I: therefore speak what thou knowest. 34 Let men of understanding tell me, and let a wise man hearken unto me. 35 Job hath spoken without knowledge, and his words were without wisdom. 36 My desire is that Job may be tried unto the end because of his answers for wicked men. 37 For he addeth rebellion unto his sin, he clappeth his hands among us, and multiplieth his words against God."

34.30.1.en: But hath any said unto God:

34.30.2.en: I have borne chastisement, I will not offend any more [31].

34.30.3.en: Elihu demands that he return to God, and in a spirit of repentance say: I have borne the chastisement, I will not sin any more!

34.30.4.en: The conclusion came bearing more violence than all the speeches of the three friends, but it seems that Elihu's intention and sincere zeal are what distinguished him from them, for he did not share their envy.

34.30.5.en: Some translate it: "Surely it is fitting to say to God: I have been chastised, I will not disobey any more." Thus Elihu demands that he walk in a spirit of humility before God.

34.30.6.en: It is fitting for the suffering man to go beyond the limits of pain to meet God in a spirit of humility and understanding, without murmuring or complaint, realizing that behind the pain is a divine plan for his edification. He presented to him a general truth, that it is fitting for the sufferer to come to know God's plan toward him.

34.30.7.en: "I have borne": some hold that the Hebrew word here means "I repented" or "chastisement," so I will not do corruption any more. Thus sufferings become a way of reviewing the soul and seeking reform by returning to God.

34.30.8.en: Indeed Job said so to God (Job 40:3-5; Mic 7:9; Lev 26:41).

34.30.9.en: That which I see not teach thou me.

34.31.0.en: If I have done iniquity, I will do no more? [32]

34.31.1.en: Elihu presents to us a wonderful picture of repentance, and at the same time brings out what is within him concerning Job.

34.31.2.en: Job was not, as his friends had said to him before, a hypocrite covering his sins with deceptive formalities and hiding his buried evils with displays of giving and service; rather he says to him: "There are in your life - as in the life of every believer - sins hidden from your eyes, which you practice involuntarily, which you cannot see or perceive. Ask God and He will reveal them to you."

34.31.3.en: God teaches His people (Job 10:2), giving them inner knowledge even of their faults which they had not perceived if they come to Him repentant (Ps 32:8; 19:12; 139:23-24).

34.31.4.en: It is fitting for the believer to set in his heart that if the Lord reveals his sins to him, he will not return to them again (Prov 28:13; Eph 4:22).

34.31.5.en: Will He recompense it according to thy mind, saying:

34.31.6.en: Because thou hast refused? thou choosest, and not I.

34.32.1.en: This text came out obscure, so the interpretations differ. Some hold that God will recompense for the deed whether the person accepts it or refuses, and that God does not act according to man's point of view, but as He sees what is right and profitable, so man should not expect God to consult men and act according to their opinions or feelings.

34.32.2.en: It is as though man says to God: Do You, O God, work as You see fit; it is You who choose and take, not I, You work and speak as You know. As for me, for my part I trust in Your decisions and submit to Your plan.

34.33.0.en: Let men of understanding tell me, and let a wise man hearken unto me: [34]

34.33.1.en: Elihu wishes to enter into dialogue with men of understanding and wisdom, because he wishes to find one who will listen to him and weigh his words and evaluate them.

34.34.0.en: Job hath spoken without knowledge, and his words were without wisdom [35].

34.34.1.en: Elihu sees in Job that he has kept silent, so he counted him rigid in his thought, holding fast to his will and to himself, so there was no profit in speaking with him. He counted him as one without knowledge or wisdom.

34.35.0.en: My desire is that Job may be tried unto the end because of his answers for wicked men [36].

34.35.1.en: Elihu wishes to bring Job to a just trial, so that his words and concepts may be tested, for he gave his answers to the men of iniquity (his friends), and he must correct what he said.

34.35.2.en: For he addeth rebellion unto his sin.

34.36.0.en: He clappeth his hands among us, and multiplieth his words against God [37].

34.36.1.en: Besides his former sins, he added a graver sin during his dialogue, namely the sin of complaint with murmuring against God. If God permitted him chastisement for his sins, he ought not to have murmured, even if his friends provoked him with unjust and violent accusations.

34.36.2.en: [Clapping] is either a sign of approval and victory, or of anger and distress (Num 24:10), or of mockery (Job 27:23). It seems that he is speaking here of clapping as a symbol of contempt and mockery of his friends' concepts. It is as though Job - instead of studying matters objectively, in a calm spirit and with a desire to know the truth and benefit from it - had all that occupied him in making light of his friends who accuse him unjustly.

34.36.3.en: "And multiplieth his words against God": instead of resorting to God for His support, he ascribed injustice to God, and went on at length in it.

34.36.4.en: Grant me the spirit of discernment!

34.36.5.en: * Grant me from You the spirit of discernment, O Wisdom of God.

34.36.6.en: So that by Your Spirit I may test every thought and every word and every action.

34.36.7.en: Let me test my words, so that no idle word comes out.

34.36.8.en: Let me test what I listen to, so that I do not waste my time with idle words.

34.36.9.en: Let me hear Your voice in everything, in Your holy Gospel, in beautiful nature, and in past and present events.

34.36.10.en: * In You I experience virtue and delight in it. In You I cannot bear evil, nor converse with it.

34.36.11.en: Let the deceitful wisdom of the world not deceive me, nor the winds of vain philosophy move me.

34.36.12.en: Let me taste Your wisdom, Your love and Your care all the day long, so that my soul rejoices even in the midst of the flames of trials.

34.36.13.en: * Grant me the spirit of discernment, so that men's praise does not deceive me, nor their sharp criticism crush me.

34.36.14.en: Rather in You let me know the divine truth and live it!

34.36.15.en: Let me hear Your voice in my depths, as in Your Church!

34.36.16.en: Let me enjoy You in the midst of Your children!

34.36.17.en: * Grant me the spirit of discernment, that I may welcome Your pure word and hold fast to it, that I may listen to You through Your servants and reject the voice of deceivers.

34.36.18.en: In You let me become a skilled money-changer, distinguishing true coins from counterfeit!

34.36.19.en: * Grant me the spirit of discernment, that I may realize that no one is perfect but You, in You let me be perfect and holy!

34.36.20.en: In You I long for the whole world to cleave to Your righteousness.

34.36.21.en: So that mankind becomes perfect and good in You!

34.36.22.en: * Grant me the spirit of discernment, so that in the midst of affliction and in the bitterness of my soul, I do not think that righteousness does not profit its possessor, nor that evil does not harm its doer.

34.36.23.en: Let me not ask: Where is Your care for Your believers?

34.36.24.en: Nor weigh matters with human, temporal scales.

34.36.25.en: Rather let me trust in Your love, Your care and Your justice.

34.36.26.en: Let me wait, for tomorrow the secrets of Your wisdom will be revealed!

34.36.27.en: * By Your dwelling in my heart, it expands to embrace every man with love.

34.36.28.en: It expands, and is not narrowed before any trial. And all trials turn to my good.

34.36.29.en: Let me perceive the secret of Your love behind every affliction!

34.36.30.en: In the midst of sufferings my soul rejoices in You, and sings always of Your righteousness!

34.36.31.en: My soul will not be troubled by the cruelty of the wicked toward me, nor do I fear the rod of sinners, for it will not rest upon me.

34.36.32.en: I bear witness to Your righteousness, You who show no partiality!

34.36.33.en: * I see You as a Father who has compassion on me as on Your son.

34.36.34.en: You do not forget a cup of cold water that I offer in Your name.

34.36.35.en: I see evils passing quickly, and my soul rejoices in Your hands as they wipe away my tears.

34.36.36.en: * Grant me the spirit of discernment, that I may realize Your care for me, Your creature.

34.36.37.en: If a man does not bear an insult that touches those subject to him, will You not care for me, Your creature and the work of Your hands?

34.36.38.en: In Your mercy You brought me into being, O Almighty, wonderful Father, so how would You not care for me with Your love?!

34.36.39.en: You gave me life by a breath from You, so how very dear I am to You?!

34.36.40.en: Will You not open Your fatherly arms to me?

34.36.41.en: * You created me from nothing, so I am the work of Your hands.

34.36.42.en: You loved me and created me, and redeemed me freely with Your precious blood; would You then let injustice befall me, O Lover of mankind?

34.36.43.en: * Let my body return to the dust from which it was created, but will my spirit not return to You, for it is a breath from Your mouth?!

34.36.44.en: You took my body by Your Incarnation, and hope returned to me that I shall not perish.

34.36.45.en: I look forward to the day of my resurrection, when my body will be glorified with my spirit!

34.36.46.en: * Your Spirit carries me from glory to glory, lifts me from the dunghill and the dust, and takes me away to heaven!

34.36.47.en: So what can the events of the world do to me?!

34.36.48.en: * Grant me the spirit of discernment, that I may realize that with You there is no partiality!

34.36.49.en: You will not show partiality to a rich man because of his wealth or his authority.

34.36.50.en: Nor will You show partiality to a people because of the multitude of its number.

34.36.51.en: Nor will You show partiality to an army because of its military capabilities.

34.36.52.en: Rather You care for every man as if there were no one else on earth.

34.36.53.en: And You care for all without distinction or bias!

34.36.54.en: * Your eyes watch every man, not to destroy him but to save him.

34.36.55.en: Your eyes behold what is in the mind and the heart.

34.36.56.en: You have no need of anyone's testimony, for everything is open before You!

34.36.57.en: * In Your love You do not wish the destruction of anyone, but deliberately the wicked insisted on turning away from You.

34.36.58.en: They left You and held Your commandment in contempt.

34.36.59.en: So evil reigned over their hearts.

34.36.60.en: Violence became their constitution, and their ears were struck with deafness, so they do not hear the cries of the wronged poor.

34.36.61.en: But You continue to hear the groans of inner hearts.

34.36.62.en: You lift them up, uphold them and glorify them!

34.36.63.en: * Is there no man who can insult a ruler or a king?

34.36.64.en: Then who dares to condemn Your divine plans?

34.36.65.en: You are King of kings! You are Lord of lords!

34.36.66.en: Your eyes are on the ways of all mankind. They look even into what is in our hearts and thoughts.

34.36.67.en: As if You had no work but to care for the sons of men.

34.36.68.en: You desire that all be saved, and come to the knowledge of You!

34.36.69.en: * Let the world rise against me, for its Creator embraces me.

34.36.70.en: Let the wicked rage with all their strength. Their spirit goes out and they return to their dust.

34.36.71.en: They mock me, and they become a spectacle, a proverb and a derision!

34.36.72.en: They turned away from You with their hard hearts, and lost their life and their glory!

34.36.73.en: * They mocked the cries of the afflicted, and did not realize that You listen to the groaning of their hearts.

34.36.74.en: They hid their faces from the wronged, and did not realize that You Yourself look upon them.

34.36.75.en: They thought the poor were tares that burn, and did not realize that You make them gold refined by fire.

34.36.76.en: * Grant me the spirit of discernment, that I may grasp the secrets of Your plans, and learn how to converse with You, and distinguish between heavenly and earthly things.

34.36.77.en: And let me hasten to You, and enjoy You within me.

34.36.78.en: * Finally, teach me and train me, that I may learn by the spirit of discernment how to speak with You!
